_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live. Since #2996 a citation that names a `#N` must name an issue that is still OPEN: the gate reads `gh issue view` for every currently-lit alarm's citation and flags a dead reference, because a citation string is not an owner (measured 2026-08-22: 4 of 7 entries pointed at closed issues, 3 of them on lit alarms). A citation with NO `#N` is never flagged by that check — a dated, self-clearing state is honestly cited in prose — but the 14-day `issueless_ancient_reds` rule still forces a `#N` past that tenure. PRUNE an entry when its alarm recovers.

token-alarm-genesis-window-active.citation: dated self-clearing window, expires 2026-08-24 — no issue, by design
token-alarm-genesis-window-active.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996): the previous citation #2116 closed 2026-08-07 'partial'. This alarm is CORRECT and needs no owner: `lambdas/common/token_alarm_window.py` sets TOKEN_ALARM_GENESIS_WINDOW = ('2026-08-16', '2026-08-24'), a dated window around the cycle-14 genesis (2026-08-17), and the 1/0 gauge is 1 for its duration by construction. It SELF-CLEARS on 2026-08-24 with no deploy and no manual step; prune this entry then. Deliberately prose rather than a `#N` — filing an issue for a designed, dated state would be manufacturing an owner for something that is working. If it is still lit after 2026-08-24, that IS a defect and needs one.

cost-metric-drift-sustained.note: Expected RED from ~7 days after its first deploy: the alarm states a true, known condition. Re-measured live 2026-08-24T23:59Z governor cycle (most recent at time of check): ratio 1.3710 — lowest since 08-21, continuing the slow pullback from the 1.4177 peak on 08-22/23, but still ~19% above the 1.15 bar; 19 consecutive 8h datapoints since box 2 landed (08-19) are ALL above bar, none sub-1.15. CE reconciliation re-measured 2026-08-25: Bedrock UnblendedCost $83.32 MTD vs self-reported LifePlatform/AI EstimatedCostUSD $61.36 MTD, a $21.96 gap (26.4%) — down $0.75 from the prior $22.71/27.4% reading a day earlier. The golden-eval AiCostTelemetry grant (previously staged) is now CONFIRMED APPLIED live (aws iam get-role-policy shows the statement; simulate-principal-policy returns allowed for cloudwatch:PutMetricData/LifePlatform/AI; infra/iam/README.md updated) but has not yet moved the ratio — golden-brief-eval.yml runs weekly (next 2026-08-31) and no run has executed since the grant applied. The dominant unattributed residual remains interactive Claude Code dev-session usage (out of scope per #3070's design — never reaches the ADR-062 chokepoint), still unsized. The alarm itself (cost-metric-drift-sustained, operational_stack.py, #2948) was re-audited this pass and found already correctly configured — threshold/window/routing all verified against DRIFT_RATIO_BAR, no alarm-side change needed. Remove this entry when box 2 lands the ratio < 1.15 for a full week AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

budget-tier-sustained-7d.note: RE-CUT 2026-08-23 (#2989, chose Option A over Option C): threshold moved from tier >= 1 sustained to tier >= 2 sustained in cdk/stacks/monitoring_stack.py — merged but NOT YET DEPLOYED (this worktree cannot cdk deploy). ADR-133 derived the permanent $150 base FROM a measured steady state ($4.12/day = 82.4% of $150) that lands inside band 1 (73-87%), so a threshold=1 alarm fired continuously on the platform's DESIGNED steady state from 2026-08-12 (17+ consecutive days) — the same background-noise failure #1927 was filed to prevent, one band up. Band 2 (reader narratives paused) is not the designed state at ~81% MTD spend, so a full week pinned there is genuinely rare and worth answering; #1927's own amendment already moved the two CI gates out of band 1, leaving only five internal/dev features there. EXPECTED POST-DEPLOY: this alarm should clear once `cdk deploy LifePlatformMonitoring` ships the new threshold, because live BudgetTier has not sustained >= 2 for a full week. Re-read the live CloudWatch alarm state after that deploy — if it has NOT cleared, that is new information (tier has been at 2+ longer than assumed here) and this entry should stay with an updated note; if it HAS cleared, prune this entry once it has been OK longer than the #2912 72h flap window.

qa-smoke-failures.citation: #3202 (cross_surface:weight) + #3204 (reader_truth:plausibility glucose) — the dated self-clearing window is RESOLVED EARLY, not expired
qa-smoke-failures.note: RE-CITED 2026-08-26T19:00Z on measured evidence, one cycle before the previous window's 2026-08-27T19:00Z expiry. The prior citation's theory — that the coach-v2 truncation fix would let the nutrition narrative publish and clear cross_surface:weight — is now FALSIFIED rather than merely unexpired, so it was replaced instead of being allowed to ride to its deadline. The 2026-08-26 17:00Z brief measured truncation WARNs at 0 (from 13-14/brief; the #3192 cap fix works, wire-recorded on #3190), yet nutrition_coach still failed BOTH attempts at score 28 / number_grounding=ungrounded on full untruncated text. Dr. Marcus Webb IS the nutrition coach (lambdas/intelligence/expert_personas.py) — so the gate holding nutrition is exactly why Webb's stale '321.0 lb' never regenerates and cross_surface:weight stays red. Causal chain, fully measured: grounding hold (#3202) -> Webb narrative not republished -> headline weight disagrees vs cockpit 326.0 -> this alarm. #3083 (open, gate:owner) remains the POLICY owner for hold-vs-fail-open and now has clean, unconfounded evidence attached. SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAILURE on the same alarm since the 2026-08-26T18:31Z nightly: reader_truth:plausibility on /api/glucose (finding e5eafd) — CGM glucose stopped landing after 08-24 while HAE rows keep arriving, filed as #3204 (the #3111 recurrence, different shape). Both must clear before this alarm goes OK; prune this entry only when both issues close AND the alarm is live-OK.

qa-smoke-warnings.note: RECONCILED 2026-08-24 (#2997, closed): the metric and the run's own log were never in conflict. 8-day reconciliation (2026-08-16..08-24) of every LifePlatform/QaSmoke WarnCount datapoint against the qa-smoke log group's `[QA] WARN` lines: 336 WARN lines total, 313 tagged [chronic] (routed to ChronicWarnCount, correctly non-alarmed per #1958) and 23 non-chronic (correctly alarmed) — every nonzero WarnCount datapoint matches a run that logged that many non-[chronic] WARN lines, exactly as qa_check.split_warns()/emf_summary_line() are written to do. #2997's original '28h window read all-chronic' observation was a sampling artifact (most qa-smoke invocations that day happened to be chronic-only), not a leak. Single producer confirmed (qa_check.emf_summary_line, called once per run from qa_smoke_lambda.lambda_handler) — no second-producer dimension needed. The alarm is not latched: describe-alarm-history shows it flapping OK<->ALARM repeatedly and reaching OK for multi-hour stretches (e.g. 2026-08-22 18:28->23:49 ~5h15m OK, 2026-08-23 23:49->2026-08-24 10:10 ~10h21m OK), contradicting the 'lit continuously since 08-20' framing. Of the non-chronic classes seen in the window: `character:receipt_replay`'s drift warn was already fixed by #2670/PR#2885 (deployed 2026-08-18 19:34 PT — chronic=True now, in the AST-guarded SANCTIONED_CHRONIC_SITES registry) and stopped appearing after that deploy; `mcp:get_todoist_snapshot`'s 'No Todoist data available' warn fired 3x on 08-17/08-18 only and has not recurred — left alarmed (no known-recurring basis to reclassify, #1958's default-False safety direction). The CURRENT, dominant, ongoing non-chronic source is `reader_truth:verdict`/`reader_truth:confirm` — genuinely different, evolving content-truth findings each time (this is the alarm doing its job, not a defect; findings are not a 'known-recurring timing' condition so #1958's chronic contract correctly keeps them alarmed). Three specific reader_truth findings recurred in the window: Home-hero temporal framing (539c6d, 08-16..08-23) — fixed by #3066/PR#3075 (merged 2026-08-23 22:35Z), no recurrence since; /api/sleep_detail interleave (fcd7d5, 08-20/08-21) — fixed by #2921 (closed 2026-08-23), no recurrence since; /api/glucose as_of_date catch-up gap (e5eafd, 08-24) — OPEN, filed as #3111 (live-checked: the DDB gap the check caught had already closed by the time #3111 was filed, reading as a transient ingestion catch-up lag rather than a stalled pipeline; #3111 owns determining whether it recurs). Citation re-pointed to #3111 as the live, open, named cause.

weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.citation: arming transition of the #2820 dead-man 2026-08-21 — not a delivery failure
weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.note: Kept 2026-08-22 (#2996). The alarm is OK, but #2912's flap check reads a 72h window and this alarm's only episode is inside it: describe-alarm-history shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> ALARM at 2026-08-21 20:44 PT and ALARM -> OK at 21:44 PT — one hour, immediately after #2820 deployed the WeeklySignalSent dead-man (treat_missing=BREACHING, so a freshly created alarm with no datapoints is ALARM by construction until the first one lands). No signal was missed. THE PRUNE RULE, corrected: remove a recovered alarm's entry once it has been OK for longer than the flap window (72h), not the moment it clears — pruning on recovery alone trades a stale entry for a flap-gate red, which is what happened while writing this. Prune after 2026-08-24 21:44 PT if still OK.

budget-tier-unreadable.note: New alarm (2026-08-23, DIL-036 slice of #2824): fires when budget_guard logs BUDGET_TIER_UNREADABLE on the public site-api-ai path — the SSM budget-tier read failed (ParameterNotFound / AccessDenied / outage), website_ai is failing CLOSED (readers get the honest 'paused' output), and the rest of the fleet is running fail-open with NO ceiling enforcement. Never a routine state: if lit, restore the SSM param/grant (/life-platform/budget-tier) — the guard recovers within one 5-min cache TTL. Prune this entry only if the alarm is retired; while #2824 is open it is the named owner.

Cleared on its own both times. The #2892 CallerClass dimension (deployed 2026-08-24) separates dev/CI spend from prod-class going forward, which removes this alarm's dev-session false-fire mode. Expiry: if it fires on a NON-dev day, investigate fresh.

life-platform-s3-bucket-size-high.citation: #2799 — DIL-026 S3 lifecycle lane, fix landed 2026-08-24 (pending post-merge apply)
life-platform-s3-bucket-size-high.note: BucketSizeBytes crossed 50GiB (54.6GB) on 2026-08-22. Live sizing (2026-08-24) found deploys/ dominates (41.5GB noncurrent, but its #2642 rule is live and correctly configured — a 7-day rolling-window artifact of routine deploy velocity, not a gap) and imports/ was a real gap (2.07GB, zero coverage). Fix: imports/ lifecycle coverage added (deploy/s3_lifecycle.json) + declared-vs-live drift assertion (deploy/drift_sentinel.py::check_s3_lifecycle) + threshold re-derived 50GB→65GiB from the measured ~52-55GB steady state (ADR-105). Two post-merge steps required before this clears: `bash deploy/apply_s3_lifecycle.sh` (imports/ rule; out-of-IaC, cdk deploy does not touch it) and `bash deploy/cdk_deploy.sh LifePlatformMonitoring` (new threshold). Expect clear within ~24-48h of both landing (next BucketSizeBytes daily period + imports/ lifecycle sweep). Re-check before pruning this citation.
